tools.name: eslint
tools.note: bundled fallback config; dropped 4 results: module_b.mjs no-await-in-loop (sequential batched DELETE is intentional), n/no-unsupported-features Object.hasOwn (range >=16.0.0 comes from the fallback config; the project declares no engines), no-unused-vars _next on module_b.mjs and module_e.mjs (Express error handlers need four parameters)

findings.title: JWT signing key hardcoded in source
findings.why: The key that signs every session token is a literal in the file, so anyone with the repository, an image or a log of it can mint a token with any `sub` and `role`; the leak happens at commit, so reachability does not matter (X-SEV-04).
findings.fix: const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET; if (!JWT_SECRET) throw new Error('JWT_SECRET is not set'); and rotate the leaked value.
findings.cite: CWE-798; OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures; OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet

findings.title: bcrypt.compare result not awaited: login accepts any password
findings.why: `bcrypt.compare` returns a Promise, which is always truthy, so `!valid` is never true and every request that names an existing email gets a token. Any anonymous caller can sign in as any user (C1 auth bypass, R1: /login is open).
findings.fix: const valid = await bcrypt.compare(password, user.password_hash);
findings.cite: CWE-287; OWASP A07:2021; ECMA-262 ToBoolean (a Promise is truthy); bcrypt README (compare is async)

findings.title: Search term interpolated into SQL text
findings.why: `q` comes from the query string and is placed inside the SQL string; schema `maxLength: 64` does not neutralise injection. Any self-registered user (signup is open) can send `%' OR ...` / UNION payloads and read or change any table the role can reach (C1/R1).
findings.fix: WHERE status = 'active' AND display_name ILIKE $1 ... [`%${q.replace(/[\\%_]/g, '\\$&')}%`, limit]
findings.cite: CWE-89; OWASP A03:2021 Injection; OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet; node-postgres docs, Queries (parameterized query)

findings.title: Admin usage route registered before the auth and role middleware
findings.why: Express runs middleware in registration order. This route sits above `app.use('/api', authenticate)` (line 92) and `app.use('/api/admin', requireRole('admin'))` (line 93), so GET /api/admin/teams/:teamId/usage answers anonymous callers with any team's usage data (C1 broken access control / R1). The sibling admin routes below the guards are protected; this one is not.
findings.fix: Move the app.get('/api/admin/teams/:teamId/usage', ...) registration below the two app.use guards (and add a team-membership check if admins are per team).
findings.cite: CWE-862; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control; Express docs, Using middleware (order of middleware loading is important)

findings.title: Document deleted by id with no ownership check
findings.evidence: const { rowCount } = await pool.query('DELETE FROM documents WHERE id = $1', [req.params.id]);
findings.why: Any authenticated user can DELETE /api/documents/:id for a document they neither own nor share: the query filters on the id alone, while the search route above scopes by `owner_id`/share. UUIDs are not authorization (C1 other users' data destroyed / R1).
findings.fix: await pool.query('DELETE FROM documents WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2', [req.params.id, req.user.sub]); return 404 on rowCount 0.
findings.cite: CWE-639; CWE-862; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control; OWASP IDOR Prevention Cheat Sheet

findings.title: bcrypt.hashSync blocks the event loop on signup
findings.why: A cost-12 hash takes on the order of 100-250 ms of synchronous CPU; /signup is open to anyone, so a handful of concurrent requests stalls every other request on the process (C2/R1).
findings.fix: const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);
findings.cite: Node.js docs, "Don't Block the Event Loop (or the Worker Pool)"; bcrypt README (async API)

findings.title: 500 response returns err.message and err.stack
findings.evidence: return reply.code(500).send({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack });
findings.why: Any database error other than 23505 (a connection failure, a constraint or syntax error) is sent to the caller with its message and stack trace, exposing table and column names, driver version and file paths to anyone who can reach /signup (C2 information exposure / R1).
findings.fix: req.log.error({ err }, 'signup failed'); return reply.code(500).type('application/problem+json').send({ type: 'about:blank', title: 'Internal Server Error', status: 500 });
findings.cite: CWE-209; OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration; OWASP Error Handling Cheat Sheet; RFC 9457

findings.title: Lost updates: += await inside Promise.all drops all but one meter
findings.evidence: subtotalCents += await meterChargeCents(teamId, meter, start, end);
findings.why: `subtotalCents` is read before each await, so the three concurrent callbacks each add to 0 and the last write wins. With meter charges 1000, 2000 and 3000 cents the subtotal is whichever resolves last, not 6000; every invoice is under-billed (C1 money wrong / R2: admin-only endpoint, so major).
findings.fix: const parts = await Promise.all(METERS.map((m) => meterChargeCents(teamId, m, start, end))); const subtotalCents = parts.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
findings.cite: CWE-362; CWE-367; ESLint docs, require-atomic-updates

findings.title: Invoice total computed with floating point dollars
findings.why: `Math.round((cents / 100) * 1.0825 * 100) / 100` rounds a binary float: for subtotalCents = 6200 the exact taxed total is 67.115 and the code returns 67.11, not 67.12 (checked in Node; 12 of the first 200,000 cent values are off by a cent). The value is stored in invoices.amount_due, and the code mixes cents (subtotalCents) with dollars (amountDue). Admin-gated, so major.
findings.fix: Keep integers: const amountDueCents = Math.round(subtotalCents * 10825 / 10000) (or BigInt/decimal) and store cents.
findings.cite: ECMA-262 Number type (IEEE 754 binary64); Stripe API docs, Currencies (amounts in the smallest unit); CWE-682; CWE-1339

findings.title: Pooled client released only on success: leaked on every error or timeout
findings.why: `client.release()` follows the queries inside `try` with no `finally`. When the query throws (including the 57014 timeout this route is built to handle) the function returns from the catch and the client is never released, so after pool-size failures every request on the service waits for a connection (C2 outage / R1: any authenticated user hits /api/search).
findings.fix: Wrap in try { ... } finally { client.release(); } and reset statement_timeout with SET LOCAL inside a transaction, or pass the timeout per query.
findings.cite: node-postgres docs, Pooling (a checked-out client must be released); CWE-772; CWE-404

findings.title: Wrong-key test asserts only inside a catch that fetch never reaches
findings.why: `fetch` resolves on HTTP 401, it does not throw, so the `catch` block (and its `expect(err.status)`) never runs: the test passes whatever the server does, including accepting the forged token. It is the only test of the invalid-signature path on the DELETE route.
findings.fix: const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'DELETE', headers }); expect(response.status).toBe(401);
findings.cite: Jest docs, Expect (expect.assertions) and Testing Asynchronous Code; WHATWG Fetch Standard (the promise rejects only on network errors)

findings.title: it.only narrows the whole file to one test
findings.evidence: it.only('adds up every meter before tax', async () => {
findings.why: Jest runs only this test; the other six tests in the file, including the authentication, rounding, failure and SMTP tests, are silently skipped while the run reports green. Jest does not reject .only in CI.
findings.fix: Remove .only.
findings.cite: Jest docs, test.only; ESLint plugin jest, no-focused-tests

findings.title: Unawaited .resolves assertion in a synchronous test
findings.why: The test function is not async and the `expect(...).resolves` promise is neither awaited nor returned, so the test finishes before the assertion runs and passes even if `amountDue` is wrong. It is the only test of the tax rounding (and, with the 64.95 expectation, a float-rounding regression would go unseen).
findings.fix: it('rounds ...', async () => { await expect(computeInvoice(...)).resolves.toMatchObject({ amountDue: 64.95 }); });
findings.cite: Jest docs, .resolves (return or await the assertion)

findings.title: console.log left in the login handler
findings.why: Unleveled output on a request path that runs on every login: it bypasses the Fastify logger, its levels and its redaction. It logs only the user id and status, not secrets, so it stays minor (X-SEV-07).
findings.fix: Delete it, or use request.log.debug({ userId: user.id }, 'login') without the status.
findings.cite: CWE-532; CWE-489; OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet

findings.title: return mailer.sendMail() inside try without await bypasses the catch
findings.why: The Promise is returned before it settles, so an SMTP rejection skips `catch`: the warning is never logged and the function rejects instead of returning null, which its callers (`info !== null`) and its own test expect. The admin quota-warning route then answers 500 instead of `{ sent: false }`. Admin-gated, so minor (C2/R2).
findings.fix: return await mailer.sendMail({ ... });
findings.cite: ECMA-262 async function return semantics; typescript-eslint, return-await; CWE-252

findings.title: dueAt computed with setUTCMonth(+1) overflows at month end
findings.why: Issuing an invoice on Jan 31 gives dueAt = Mar 3 (checked in Node: 2026-01-31 becomes 2026-03-03), and Oct 31 gives Dec 1; the wrong due date is stored on the invoice. Only month-end issue dates are affected and the route is admin-gated, so minor (C2/R2).
findings.fix: Clamp the day: set the date to the 1st of next month, then min(originalDay, daysInThatMonth), or use a date library.
findings.cite: MDN, Date.prototype.setMonth (overflow rolls into the next month); CWE-682

findings.title: Loose equality between a status string and a string literal
findings.why: `status` is a string column compared with a string literal, so coercion cannot change the result (X-SEV-08): reader cost only.
findings.fix: if (user.status === 'disabled') {
findings.cite: ECMA-262 IsLooselyEqual; ESLint docs, eqeqeq

findings.title: Commented-out token issuance left in
findings.evidence: // const token = jwt.sign({ id: user.id }, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '7d' });
findings.why: Dead code that readers cannot tell from a plan or a warning (it also records a 7-day expiry that the live code does not use); version control keeps the old code.
findings.fix: Delete the line; if the decision matters, replace it with one sentence saying why the TTL is 1h.
findings.cite: Martin, Clean Code ch. 4, Commented-Out Code; SonarSource rule S125

findings.title: Unused import randomUUID
findings.why: `randomUUID` is imported but never used (reader cost only).
findings.fix: Remove the import.
findings.cite: ESLint docs, no-unused-vars

findings.title: Fixed port 4100 for the test server
findings.why: A fixed port collides when suites run in parallel or on a busy CI host (test-code runtime problem, so D3 nit).
findings.fix: server = app.listen(0); const { port } = server.address(); and build BASE_URL from it.
findings.cite: Martin Fowler, Eradicating Non-Determinism in Tests; Node.js docs, server.listen (port 0)
